newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Treasury official retracts "selfishness" charge.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Treasury official retracts "selfishness" charge.

text.p: A senior Treasury Department official who charged that "selfishness" lay behind a Congressional bid to scrap inheritance taxes withdrew his remark under fire Wednesday.

As criticism erupted over comments made on Monday by Deputy Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers, the Clinton administration decided to back down for fear the issue could poison efforts to reach a budget deal with the Republican-controlled Congress.

"I should not have used the term selfishness to characterise positions in the debate over estate taxes," Summers said in a brief meeting with reporters. "There is room for honest disagreement on this issue."
Summers told reporters on Monday that evidence presented by Congress for repealing estate taxes "is about as bad as it gets" and could only arise from selfish motives.
It came at the beginning of a critical week for negotiations between the White House and Congress on reaching a budget pact and drew the approbation of both sides as well as the business community.
Senate Majority leader Trent Lott warned Tuesday that Summers' comments might make it more difficult to reach a comprehensive budget pact.

"It is not constructive to have a sub-cabinet level official using the word selfish to describe supporters of death tax reform at a time when we're trying to forge a bipartisan budget agreement with the President," Lott said.

A major business lobby group, The National Association of Manufacturers (NAM), issued a scathing statement saying Summers' remarks demonstrated a callous White House attitude toward small businesses' concerns.
"Trying to preserve a family business from the ravages of estate taxes isn't selfishness, it's economic survival," NAM vice-president Paul Huard said.
